'''''Rogue Squadron''''' is an upcoming ''[[Star Wars]]'' film.<ref name="Announcement" /> It will be directed by [[Wikipedia:Wonder Woman (2017 film)|''Wonder Woman'']] director [[Patty Jenkins]].<ref name="Announcement" />

==Publisher's summary==
''The next ''Star Wars'' feature film will be'' Rogue Squadron'' — directed by Patty Jenkins (''Wonder Woman'' franchise). The story will introduce a new generation of starfighter pilots as they earn their wings and risk their lives in a boundary-pushing, high-speed thrill-ride, and move the saga into the future era of the galaxy.''

''Lock S-foils in attack position: ''Rogue Squadron'' arrives in theaters Christmas 2023.''<ref name="Announcement" />

==Development==
===Initial reveals===
{{Quote|When ''[my father]'' lost his life in service to ''[the United States]'', it ignited a desire in me to turn all of that tragedy and thrill into one day making the greatest fighter pilot movie of all time. But try as I might and look as I did, I couldn't find the right story ever. I kept looking and looking, but I just couldn't find the right one. Now I found a story about two things I love.|Patty Jenkins|<ref name="Jenkins Investor Video">{{Twitter|PattyJenks|status/1337177394625478656|[[Patty Jenkins]]|date=2020-12-10|quote=When [my father] lost his life in service to [the United States], it ignited a desire in me to turn all of that tragedy and thrill into one day making the greatest fighter pilot movie of all time. But try as I might and look as I did, I couldn't find the right story ever. I kept looking and looking, but I just couldn't find the right one. Now I found a story about two things I love.|archivedate=20230321072036}}</ref>}}
''Rogue Squadron'' was first announced during a [[The Walt Disney Company|Disney]] investor's broadcast on [[December 10]], [[2020]] where [[Lucasfilm]] President [[Kathleen Kennedy]] revealed the film's title, release date, and director, Patty Jenkins.<ref name="Investor 2020 Showcase">{{DisneyCompany|url=disney-investor-day-2020|text=Disney Investor Day 2020}}</ref> At the same time as the broadcast, Jenkins released a video on her [[Wikipedia:Twitter|Twitter]] account, where she discussed the film's personal connection to her, as her father was a pilot.<ref name="Jenkins Investor Video" /> On [[December 12]], Jenkins revealed that ''Rogue Squadron'' will be an entirely new and original story and not an adaptation of [[Star Wars: X-Wing (novel series)|the novel]] and [[Star Wars: Rogue Squadron (series)|video game series]].<ref name="IGN">{{WebCite|url=https://www.ign.com/articles/patty-jenkins-star-wars-rogue-squadron-movie-is-not-a-video-game-adaptation|text=Patty Jenkins' Rogue Squadron Movie Is Not a Video Game Adaptation|author=[https://www.ign.com/person/JoshuaYehl-IGN Joshua Yehl]|date=2020-12-12|work=[[Wikipedia:IGN|''IGN'']]|archivedate=20201212190041}}</ref> On [[December 14]], in an interview with [[Wikipedia:Collider (website)|''Collider'']], Jenkins revealed that the film has been in development for a long while, with a story treatment almost having been completed. She also expressed her excitement over the story, and said that a writer had been already hired for the project, but had not yet been revealed.<ref name="Collider">{{WebCite|url=https://collider.com/star-wars-rogue-squadron-script-patty-jenkins-interview|text=Patty Jenkins on 'Star Wars' Movie 'Rogue Squadron' & Who Is Writing the Script|author=[https://collider.com/author/allie-gemmill Allie Gemmill]|date=2020-12-14|work=[[Wikipedia:Collider (website)|''Collider'']]|archivedate=20230404011638}}</ref> A day later, on [[December 15]], in an interview with [[Wikipedia:Yahoo!|''Yahoo!'']], Jenkins discussed the high amount of pressure she felt to direct a ''Star Wars'' film, and how her position as the first woman director of a film in the franchise was a "groundbreaking position."<ref name="Yahoo">{{WebCite|url=https://www.yahoo.com/entertainment/patty-jenkins-star-wars-rogue-squadron-first-female-director-wonder-woman-185422594.html|text=Patty Jenkins talks groundbreaking 'Rogue Squadron' gig: 'I feel a huge amount of pressure to make a great "Star Wars" film'|author=[https://www.yahoo.com/author/kevin-polowy Kevin Polowy]|date=2020-12-15|work=[[Wikipedia:Yahoo!|''Yahoo!'']]|archivedate=20220910204448}}</ref>

On [[June 25]], [[2021]], [[Wikipedia:The Hollywood Reporter|''The Hollywood Reporter'']], via their "[https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/e/heat-vision Heat Vision]" newsletter, reported that screenwriter [[Matthew Robinson]] was attached to write the script for the film.<ref name="THR Writer" /> On [[June 29]], in an interview with the [[Wikipedia:Associated Press|Associated Press]], stated that the film would honor books from author [[Michael A. Stackpole]] in the ''Star Wars: X-Wing'' series as well as the video game series, while also bringing the story into a "new age."<ref name="AssociatedPress">{{Twitter|APEntertainment|status/1410000613753069574|[[Wikipedia:Associated Press|Associated Press]]|date=2021-06-29|quote=The Michael Stackpole books and the video games and all of the Rogue Squadron books, there's an incredible history that's really important to honor. And yet, it must be brought to a new age, because we have to tell a new story with it and so you're trying to blend the best of everything and make it the great fighter-pilot movie, which I've always wanted to make, as well. It's a big brew of things that you're trying to put together and still try to keep a simple story.|archivedate=20220826094107}}</ref>
In an interview with the news site a month later, Jenkins explained how she was developing the film with Lucasfilm: "It's an entirely different way of working. I'm on the phone with all of them and doing Zoom meetings with everybody involved in ''Star Wars'' all the time. I'm fairly free to do the story that we want to do, but you really need to know who's done what, who's doing what, where it goes and how it works, and what designs have been done before. It's a whole other way of working that I'm getting up to speed on."<ref name="Streaming">{{WebCite|url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/movies/movie-news/patty-jenkins-streamings-day-and-date-strategy-1234975282|text=Patty Jenkins Thinks Streaming's Day-and-Date Strategy Won't Last|author=Chris Gardner|date=2021-07-03|work=[[Wikipedia:The Hollywood Reporter|''The Hollywood Reporter'']]|archivedate=20210707054902}}</ref>

===Production troubles===
{{Quote|I originally left ''Rogue Squadron'' after a long and productive development process when it became clear it couldn't happen soon enough and I did not want to delay ''WW3'' any further. When I did, Lucasfilm asked me to consider coming back to ''RS'' after ''WW3'', which I was honored to do, so I agreed. They made a new deal with me. In fact, I am still on it and that project has been in active development ever since. I don't know if it will happen or not. We never do until the development process is complete, but I look forward to its potential ahead.|Patty Jenkins|<ref name="Jenkins Statement">{{Twitter|PattyJenks|status/1602824242684252161|[[Patty Jenkins]]|date=2022-12-13|quote=I originally left Rogue Squadron after a long and productive development process when it became clear it couldn't happen soon enough and I did not want to delay WW3 any further. When I did, Lucasfilm asked me to consider coming back to RS after WW3, which I was honored to do, so I agreed. They made a new deal with me. In fact, I am still on it and that project has been in active development ever since. I don't know if it will happen or not. We never do until the development process is complete, but I look forward to its potential ahead.|archivedate=20230723031210}}</ref>}}
On [[November 8]], 2021, ''The Hollywood Reporter'' reported that ''Rogue Squadron'' had originally been slated to begin production in [[2022]], but was delayed due to Patty Jenkins's commitments to other projects. Therefore, the film was officially taken off of Lucasfilm's production schedule.<ref name="THR Delay">{{WebCite|url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/movies/movie-news/patty-jenkins-star-wars-movie-rogue-squadron-delayed-1235044023|text=Patty Jenkins 'Star Wars' Movie 'Rogue Squadron' Delayed (Exclusive)|author=[https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/author/borys-kit Borys Kit]|date=2021-11-08|work=[[Wikipedia:The Hollywood Reporter|''The Hollywood Reporter'']]|archivedate=20230830154023}}</ref>

In [[May]] 2022, in an interview with [[Wikipedia:Vanity Fair (magazine)|''Vanity Fair'']], Lucasfilm president Kathleen Kennedy confirmed that ''Rogue Squadron'' had been pushed off to the side by Lucasfilm.<ref name="Vanity Fair">{{WebCite|url=https://www.vanityfair.com/hollywood/2022/05/star-wars-kathleen-kennedy|text=''Star Wars'' Forever: How Kathleen Kennedy Is Expanding the Galaxy|author=Anthony Breznican|date=2022-05-18|work=[[Wikipedia:Vanity Fair (magazine)|''Vanity Fair'']]|archivedate=20220518161304}}</ref> On [[December 13]] of the same year, Patty Jenkins released a public statement regarding her projects. In her statement, Jenkins clarified that she originally left the film after a long and productive development process which threatened to delay her next project. Jenkins stated that when she left, Lucasfilm asked her to reconsider returning once her project was complete, which she agreed to. A new deal was made and the project had been in active development as of December 2022, though Jenkins confirmed that she was not sure if it would actually happen or not.<ref name="Jenkins Statement" />

On [[March 7]], [[2023]], [[Wikipedia:Variety (magazine)|''Variety'']] reported that the film was no longer in development.<ref name="Variety Canceled">{{WebCite|url=https://variety.com/2023/film/news/star-wars-kevin-feige-patty-jenkins-movies-shelved-1235545774|text='Star Wars' Shakeup: Kevin Feige and Patty Jenkins Movies Shelved, Taika Waititi Looking to Star in His Own Film (EXCLUSIVE)|author=Adam B. Vary|date=2023-03-07|work=[[Wikipedia:Variety (magazine)|''Variety'']]|archivedate=20231125132422/}}</ref> At [[Celebration Europe (2023)|Celebration Europe 2023]], Lucasfilm president Kathleen Kennedy spoke to [[Wikipedia:IGN|''IGN'']] in an interview, saying that ''Rogue Squadron'' was a project they continue to currently discuss at Lucasfilm, and that it may remain as a film or may be transformed into a series.<ref name="IGN Celebration">{{WebCite|url=https://www.ign.com/articles/star-wars-rogue-squadron-could-still-happen-says-lucasfilm-president-kathleen-kennedy|text=Star Wars Rogue Squadron Could Still Happen, Says Lucasfilm President Kathleen Kennedy|author=Ryan Dinsdale|date=2023-04-07|work=[[Wikipedia:IGN|''IGN'']]|archiveurl=https://archive.is/JKMle}}</ref> 

===Development recommences===
{{Quote|So, when I left ''Star Wars'' to do ''Wonder Woman 3'', I thought maybe I'll come back to ''Star Wars'' after ''Wonder Woman 3''. So, we did a deal for that to happen, started a deal, but I thought I was doing ''Wonder Woman''. When that went away, Lucasfilm and I were like, oh, we gotta finish this deal. We finished the deal right as the strike was happening. So I now owe a draft of ''Star Wars'' and so we will see what happens there.|Patty Jenkins|<ref name="Jenkins Podcast">{{YouTube|video=6ualzkFkIwg|text=Talking Pictures Podcast | Episode 9 | Max|channel=@hbomax|name=HBO Max|date=2024-03-12|quote=So, when I left ''Star Wars'' to do ''Wonder Woman 3'', I thought maybe I'll come back to ''Star Wars'' after ''Wonder Woman 3''. So, we did a deal for that to happen, started a deal, but I thought I was doing ''Wonder Woman''. When that went away, Lucasfilm and I were like, oh, we gotta finish this deal. We finished the deal right as the strike was happening. So I now owe a draft of ''Star Wars'' and so we will see what happens there. You know, like, who knows? It's hard, they have a hard job in front of them of what's the first movie they're gonna do. They have other directors who have been working, but I am now, you know, I’m back on doing ''Rogue Squadron'' and we'll see what happens. We need to develop, you know, get it to where we're both super happy with it.}}</ref>}}
On [[March 12]], [[2024]], while on the ''Talking Pictures'' podcast from [[Wikipedia:Turner Classic Movies|Turner Classic Movies]], Jenkins revealed that she had signed a deal to write a new draft of ''Rogue Squadron'' for Lucasfilm the prior year, right before the beginning of the [[Wikipedia:2023 Writers Guild of America strike|2023 Writers Guild of America strike]], and still owed the company her draft. She also reiterated that she would "absolutely be happy" directing a project in the ''Star Wars'' franchise.<ref name="Jenkins Podcast" /> However, on [[October 31]], it was announced that Jenkins was actively in development on and had signed a major deal to write, direct, and produce a movie in the [[Wikipedia:Lego|Lego]] franchise for [[Wikipedia:Universal Pictures|Universal Pictures]].<ref name="Jenkins Lego">{{WebCite|url=https://deadline.com/2024/10/lego-movies-patty-jenkins-jake-kasdan-joe-cornish-1236163597|text=Jake Kasdan, Patty Jenkins & Joe Cornish Set To Helm Live-Action Lego Movies For Universal|author=Anthony D'Alessandro|date=2024-10-31|work=[[Wikipedia:Deadline_Hollywood|''Deadline'']]|archivedate=20250804180133}}</ref> Jenkins has since not commented on the status of ''Rogue Squadron'' or her attachment to the project.

In [[March]] [[2025]], Michael A. Stackpole, author of the ''X-Wing'' book series confirmed that he had exchanged "cursory notes back and forth" with Jenkins regarding the film at some point in its development, and speculated on the possibility of Jenkins using several characters from his book series,<ref name="MegStackpole">{{YouTube|video=6ztNBuKNP2U|text=Star Wars Meg 2025 Interview with Michael A. Stackpole|channel=@StarWarsMeg|name=Star Wars Meg}}</ref> referring to her comments on honoring his series back in a June 2021 interview.<ref name="AssociatedPress" /> When asked if [[Denis Lawson]] would reprise his role as [[Rogue Leader]] [[Wedge Antilles]], Stackpole said he was unsure, but assumed the film would take place after [[Star Wars: Episode IX The Rise of Skywalker|''Star Wars'': Episode IX ''The Rise of Skywalker'']], and thus Lawson would be perfect to depict Wedge at that point in the timeline.<ref name="MegStackpole" />

In [[April]] 2025, during [[Celebration Japan (2025)|Celebration Japan]], the film ''[[Star Wars: Starfighter]]'', with similar themes to that of ''Rogue Squadron'', was announced. Similar to prior rumors about ''Rogue Squadron'', the film is set to take place after the events of ''Star Wars'': Episode IX ''The Rise of Skywalker'' and is directed by [[Shawn Levy]].<ref name="Variety">{{WebCite|url=https://variety.com/2023/tv/news/shawn-levy-stranger-things-season-5-star-wars-movie-interview-1235764827|text=Shawn Levy Talks New 'Star Wars' Movie, 'Deadpool 3' and 'Stranger Things' Kids Aging: 'Our Makeup Department Is Pretty Exceptional'|archivedate=20250417182828}}</ref>

==Release and reception==
On [[May 7]], [[2019]], Disney released its 2020–[[2027]] theatrical release schedule, with a ''Star Wars'' film scheduled for [[December 16]], 2022.<ref name="Variety Disney 2019">{{WebCite|url=https://variety.com/2019/film/news/disney-avatar-star-wars-marvel-1203207661|text=Disney Moves 'Avatar' Sequels, Announces New 'Star Wars' Films|author=Brent Lang and Rebecca Rubin|date=2019-05-07|work=[[Wikipedia:Variety (magazine)|''Variety'']]|archivedate=20200727083136}}</ref> ''[[The Star Wars Show]]'' also reported on the news on [[May 15]].<ref name="SW Show">{{StarWarsShow|dUSoopV7EKo|Star Wars Dates Announced, Plus We Won an Emmy!|sw_url=video/star-wars-dates-announced-plus-we-won-an-emmy}}</ref> The release date slot was originally for [[The First Jedi|the first entry]] in a [[Untitled Star Wars film series|film series]] by [[Wikipedia:Game of Thrones|''Game of Thrones'']] writers [[David Benioff]] and [[D.B. Weiss]].<ref name="Gizmodo">{{WebCite|url=https://gizmodo.com/the-first-star-wars-films-after-rise-of-skywalker-will-1834749699|text=It's Official: The First ''Star Wars'' Film After ''Rise of Skywalker'' Will Be From Game of Thrones' Showrunners|author=Beth Elderkin|date=2019-05-14|work=[[Wikipedia:Gizmodo|''Gizmodo'']]|archivedate=20210612212947}}</ref> After the pair's departure from the project, the release slot stayed on Disney's calendar and was delayed to [[December 22]], 2023 after the onset of the [[Wikipedia:COVID-19 pandemic|COVID-19 pandemic]].<ref name="Variety 2020">{{WebCite|url=https://variety.com/2020/film/box-office/star-wars-films-avatar-sequels-pushed-back-a-year-in-disney-release-calendar-shakeup-1234715104|text='Star Wars' Films, 'Avatar' Sequels Pushed Back a Year in Disney Release Calendar Shakeup|author=Rebecca Rubin|date=2020-07-23|work=[[Wikipedia:Variety (magazine)|''Variety'']]|archivedate=20200723212010}}</ref> Thereafter, the release date slot was given to ''Rogue Squadron''.<ref name="Investor 2020 Showcase" /> On [[September 15]], 2022, Disney officially removed ''Rogue Squadron'' and the release date slot from its calendar.<ref name="Variety Calendar Removal">{{WebCite|url=https://variety.com/2022/film/news/disney-star-wars-spinoff-rogue-squadron-release-snow-white-inside-out-2-lion-king-sequel-1235373972|text=Disney Removes 'Star Wars' Spinoff 'Rogue Squadron' From Release Calendar, Sets Dates for 'Snow White,' 'Inside Out 2' and 'Lion King' Sequel|author=Rebecca Rubin|date=2022-09-15|work=[[Wikipedia:Variety (magazine)|''Variety'']]|archivedate=20231130164259}}</ref>
